To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have synthesized a series of ferrocenyl thiazepine derivatives, which were characterized by X-ray diffractions and NMR and IR spectroscopy, and that these compounds have shown to have antiprotozoal activity.
the diastereoselec-tive synthesis of ferrocenyl thiazepine derivatives is reported for the first time, and that these compounds show antiprotozoal activity against Entamoeba histolytica.
the synthesis, structure, electrochemistry and biological activity of new polycyclic thiazepine derivatives have been investigated and reported for the first time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of a series of polycyclic thiazepines with ferrocene moieties, which are of interest for medicinal applications.

the synthesis of novel ferrocenyl derivatives with a thiazepine ring, which have a high potential as antimicrobial and antiparasitic drugs, as well as with the electrochemical behavior of diferrocenyl systems.

the synthesis of new ferrocene derivatives with biological activity, and the characterization of their structures by spectroscopic methods, electrochemical and theoretical studies, and the determination of their biological activities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the compounds herein described are a new type of ferrocenyl thiazepine derivatives, with interesting biological activity and electrochemical behavior.
the obtained results are promising, and that the ferrocenyl thiazepines could be considered as potential candidates for further studies as antiamoebic agents.
the compounds 4a and c are good candidates as antiparasitic agents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ferrocenyl moiety is an important structural element for the biological activity of the thiazepine derivatives.
we have developed a new synthetic strategy for the preparation of a series of polycyclic thiazepines containing the ferrocenyl moiety.
the ferrocenyl derivatives described in this study are good candidates to be tested in vivo as a new generation of anti-amoebeic drugs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ferrocene moiety in the molecules can play the role of an electron transfer mediator and/or a redox active moiety.
the ferrocenyl moiety is a good candidate for the development of new antiamoebic drugs.

ferrocenyl-containing thiazepines are easily prepared by a one-step reaction, and that their biological activities are promising for future development of drugs for the treatment of amoebic dysentery.
